body:
_Migrated from issue #1052, filed 2026-07-21._

Split out of the review on #1047 (findings 6 and 7 from the cross-family pass).

## The gap

Most `/api/v1` endpoint tests call the view function directly via
`inspect.unwrap(mod.some_view)(...)` with CSRF disabled. That exercises the
function body but not the boundary the user actually hits, so a change that
breaks the shipped endpoint can leave every test green:

- route accidentally changed from POST to GET
- blueprint registration removed
- `@csrf.exempt` added
- `@user_login_required` dropped

The same shape shows up on the frontend side: several SPA "tests" assert that a
substring appears in a `.tsx` source file. Deleting the button JSX while leaving
the hook import and a comment behind keeps them passing.

This is the unit-boundary trap the verification standard already warns about —
worth closing generically rather than per-PR.

## What would close this

1. A small authenticated app-client fixture (real `test_client`, real CSRF) that
   a route test can opt into with one line.
2. For each write endpoint, at least one test through that fixture asserting:
   the happy path over real HTTP, rejection without a CSRF token, and rejection
   when unauthenticated.
3. Replace source-substring SPA tests with RTL renders that assert the control
   appears for the right user/feature combination, click it, and check the
   submitted payload and the post-success label.

Not urgent, no user-visible symptom — this is coverage quality. Doing it once in
`conftest.py` makes it cheap for every route afterwards.

Context: #1047 verified this boundary by hand against `cwn-local` (CSRF-omitted
POST → 400, unauthenticated POST → 400) because the suite couldn't.
title: API tests bypass the HTTP boundary: routing, method and auth decorators aren't pinned
